Check why filesystem, Unix socket, network, scope, or command access would be allowed or denied

USAGE
  nono why [flags]

QUERY:
      --command <COMMAND>
          Command name to check against command policy

      --caller <CALLER>
          Caller edge for command policy checks (default: session)
          
          [default: session]

      --path <PATH>
          Path to check

      --unix-socket <PATH>
          Pathname AF_UNIX socket to check

      --socket-op <OP>
          Unix socket operation to check (default: connect)

          Possible values:
          - connect: Connect to an existing socket
          - bind:    Bind and create a socket at this path

      --lexical-profile-path
          Match absolute literal paths against profile rules without resolving them on this host

      --op <OP>
          Operation to check: read, write, or readwrite

          Possible values:
          - read:      Read-only access
          - write:     Write-only access
          - readwrite: Read and write access

      --host <HOST>
          Network host or URL to check (e.g. github.com or https://github.com/org/repo)

      --scope <SCOPE>
          Landlock scope to check

          Possible values:
          - signal:               Signal scoping
          - abstract-unix-socket: Abstract UNIX socket scoping

      --port <PORT>
          Network port (default 443)
          
          [default: 443]

      --allow-domain <DOMAIN_OR_URL>
          Add a domain to the proxy allowlist for this query (repeatable)

      --deny-domain <DOMAIN>
          Block a domain through the proxy for this query (repeatable)

  [ARGS]...
          Arguments for --command after `--`

OPTIONS:
  -s, --silent
          Silent mode - suppress all nono output (banner, summary, status)

      --theme <THEME>
          Color theme for output (mocha, latte, frappe, macchiato, tokyo-night, minimal)
          
          [env: NONO_THEME=]

      --log-file <PATH>
          Write logs to a file instead of stderr
          
          [env: NONO_LOG_FILE=]

      --json
          Output JSON instead of human-readable format

      --self
          Query current sandbox state (use inside a sandboxed process)

  -h, --help
          Print help

CONTEXT:
  -a, --allow <DIR>
          Directories to allow read+write access (for query context)

  -r, --read <DIR>
          Directories to allow read-only access (for query context)

  -w, --write <DIR>
          Directories to allow write-only access (for query context)

      --allow-file <FILE>
          Single files to allow read+write access (for query context)

      --read-file <FILE>
          Single files to allow read-only access (for query context)

      --write-file <FILE>
          Single files to allow write-only access (for query context)

      --allow-unix-socket <SOCKET>
          Exact pathname Unix sockets to allow connect access (for query context)

      --allow-unix-socket-bind <SOCKET>
          Exact pathname Unix sockets to allow connect and bind (for query context)

      --allow-unix-socket-dir <DIR>
          Direct-child pathname Unix sockets to allow in a directory (for query context)

      --allow-unix-socket-dir-bind <DIR>
          Direct-child pathname Unix sockets to allow connect and bind (for query context)

      --allow-unix-socket-subtree <DIR>
          Descendant pathname Unix sockets to allow in a subtree (for query context)

      --allow-unix-socket-subtree-bind <DIR>
          Descendant pathname Unix sockets to allow connect and bind (for query context)

      --block-net
          Block network access (for query context)

  -p, --profile <NAME>
          Use a named profile for query context

      --extends <PROFILE>
          Extend the selected profile with an additional base profile for this query

      --workdir <DIR>
          Working directory for $WORKDIR expansion in profiles


EXAMPLES
  nono why --path ~/.ssh --op read             # Check if ~/.ssh is readable
  nono why --path ./src --op write --allow .   # Check with capability context
  nono why --json --path ~/.aws --op read      # JSON output for agents
  nono why --unix-socket /run/docker.sock      # Query pathname Unix socket connect access
  nono why --host api.openai.com --port 443    # Query network access
  nono why --self --path /var --op write       # Inside sandbox, query own capabilities
  nono why --profile gh --command gh -- issue comment 1052
                                                # Query command-policy argv rules

COMMAND-POLICY DENIALS
  `nono why --command <cmd> -- <args...>` diagnoses command-policy argv rules.
  A message like:

    nono: command policy denied gh: Command 'gh' is blocked: agents may read issues but not comment on them

  is a command-policy denial from
  command_policies.commands.<name>.from.<caller>.invocation_policy. If the
  command uses proxy credentials, also check endpoint_policy for HTTP method
  and path rules.
